newsitem.title: GERMANY: German exports seen rising in coming months - Buba.
newsitem.headline: German exports seen rising in coming months - Buba.

text.p: German exports should continue to increase in the months to come amid stronger foreign demand, the Bundesbank said in its September report.

German exports rose about a real one percent in the second quarter of 1996 after six months stagnation at high levels while foreign manufacturing incoming orders were up 6.5 percent from the low hit in the last quarter of 1995.
"The extent of this discrepancy is notable. This allows one to expect a continued upward movement in exports in the coming months," the Bundesbank said.
"In any case German products' ability to compete internationally has improved markedly after the substantial easing of currency exchange rates," the report added.

Germany's current account balance ended the second quarter with a 10.5 billion mark deficit, after a four billion mark deficit in the first quarter, the Bundesbank said, attributing this to more capital investment spending and transfers abroad.

The Bundesbank said income from foreign trade was, at 23 billion marks in the second quarter of 1996, unchanged from the previous quarter, but the total "unseen" foreign trade deficit rose by 6.5 billion marks to 32.5 billion.
Imports also rose about one percent in the second quarter, both in real and unadjusted terms, the Bundesbank said.
Up-to-date data on import and export activity was unavailable, the report said.
In the four months through April, imports declined slightly but imports from European Union states rose a real 2.5 percent with Spanish imports up 11 percent and U.K. imports rising 7.5 percent.
However imports from developing countries dropped 6.5 percent and U.S. imports fell seven percent, largely due to the strengthening of the dollar, giving rise to an overall slight drop in imports.
